sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Mritsanjeevani Sura 
 It is a classical Asava (Fermented Ayurvedic Tonic) preparation and it contains many potent herbs like Vasa (Adhatoda vasica), Mochras (Bombax ceiba exudate), Lajjalu (Mimosa pudica), Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera), Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris) etc. According to Ayurveda, it is Jeevaniya (Life-promoting), Pushtikara (Nourishing), Balya (Strengthening) and nourishes all our Dhatus (Body Tissues) in chronological order. It should be strictly taken under the guidance of a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner, since its alcohol content is approximately 16%. It is really effective in chronic diseases and helps combat weakness and wasting related to it. It is also useful in reducing excess mucus in airways and promoting free flow of air in the respiratory system. 
 2. Vishalyakarni Swaras (Eupatorium triplinervis) 
 It is also called ‘Ayapaan’ in Sanskrit. It is an aromatic herb and its leaves hold many therapeutic benefits. It is Balya (Strengthening) and it acts as Raktastambhak (Hemostatic), according to Ayurveda. It is Tikta (Bitter) Kashaya (Astringent) in taste, Ushna (Hot) in potency and balances Pitta Kapha doshas. Its main active constituents are Apayanin, Carotene, Vitamin C etc. It causes local vasoconstriction and promotes coagulation at the bleeding sites. It’s also rich in anti-oxidants, due to which it protects vascular endothelium and reduces capillary fragility. 
 Method Of Preparation 
 Take 1 litre of Mritsanjeevani Sura and 1 litre of Vishalyakarni Swaras (Eupatorium triplinervis) and put them in an earthen pot together. Mix them well and cover the mouth of the pot with a cork. Leave it undisturbed in a dark room for a period of 7 days. On the 8th day, filter it and store it in clean glass bottles for future use.

sections.dosage: 10-10 drops, every three hours with 10-10 ml water.
sections.contraindications:
People with known allergy to fermented products 
 Gastric/Duodenal ulcers 
 Pregnant women 
 Breastfeeding mothers 

 Conclusion 
 Asrahararishta stands as a focused Ayurvedic formulation designed to address conditions associated with excessive blood loss while simultaneously supporting overall strength and recovery. By combining a nourishing fermented base with a potent hemostatic herbal juice, it works on both symptom control and internal rejuvenation. When used judiciously under professional supervision, Asrahararishta can play a valuable role in managing bleeding disorders and debility-related conditions, helping the body regain stability, endurance, and functional harmony.

Asrahararishta – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More 
 Introduction 
 Asrahararishta is a classical Arishta (Fermented Ayurvedic Tonic) formulation. And as its name suggests, ‘Asra’ means ‘Blood’ and ‘Har’ means ‘Relieving’, therefore it is beneficial in relieving disorders/diseases with excessive bleeding. Moreover, it focuses on restoring balance, strengthening the body, and replenishing depleted tissues. Conditions such as Raktapitta (Bleeding disorders), excessive menstrual bleeding, and blood loss associated with chronic illnesses often lead to weakness, fatigue, and gradual deterioration of bodily strength. It addresses this and rebuilds vitality from within. 
 Ingredients Their Quantity 
 
 Mritsanjeevani Sura – 1 litre 
 Vishalyakarni Swaras – 1 litre 
 
 Description Of Ingredients 
 1. Mritsanjeevani Sura 
 It is a classical Asava (Fermented Ayurvedic Tonic) preparation and it contains many potent herbs like Vasa (Adhatoda vasica), Mochras (Bombax ceiba exudate), Lajjalu (Mimosa pudica), Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera), Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris) etc. According to Ayurveda, it is Jeevaniya (Life-promoting), Pushtikara (Nourishing), Balya (Strengthening) and nourishes all our Dhatus (Body Tissues) in chronological order. It should be strictly taken under the guidance of a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner, since its alcohol content is approximately 16%. It is really effective in chronic diseases and helps combat weakness and wasting related to it. It is also useful in reducing excess mucus in airways and promoting free flow of air in the respiratory system. 
 2. Vishalyakarni Swaras (Eupatorium triplinervis) 
 It is also called ‘Ayapaan’ in Sanskrit. It is an aromatic herb and its leaves hold many therapeutic benefits. It is Balya (Strengthening) and it acts as Raktastambhak (Hemostatic), according to Ayurveda. It is Tikta (Bitter) Kashaya (Astringent) in taste, Ushna (Hot) in potency and balances Pitta Kapha doshas. Its main active constituents are Apayanin, Carotene, Vitamin C etc. It causes local vasoconstriction and promotes coagulation at the bleeding sites. It’s also rich in anti-oxidants, due to which it protects vascular endothelium and reduces capillary fragility. 
 Method Of Preparation 
 Take 1 litre of Mritsanjeevani Sura and 1 litre of Vishalyakarni Swaras (Eupatorium triplinervis) and put them in an earthen pot together. Mix them well and cover the mouth of the pot with a cork. Leave it undisturbed in a dark room for a period of 7 days. On the 8th day, filter it and store it in clean glass bottles for future use. 
 Indications

 Raktapradar (Heavy menstrual bleeding) 
 Rakta Atisaar (Bloody Diarrhea) 
 Kaas (Cough) 
 Urahkshat/Kshaya (Wasting disease) 
 Rajyakshma (Tuberculosis) 
 
 Dosage 
 10-10 drops, every three hours with 10-10 ml water. 
 Contraindications 
 
 People with known allergy to fermented products 
 Gastric/Duodenal ulcers 
 Pregnant women 
 Breastfeeding mothers

 Asrahararishta stands as a focused Ayurvedic formulation designed to address conditions associated with excessive blood loss while simultaneously supporting overall strength and recovery. By combining a nourishing fermented base with a potent hemostatic herbal juice, it works on both symptom control and internal rejuvenation.
